newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran to award buy-back oil projects by end March.
newsitem.headline: Iran to award buy-back oil projects by end March.

text.p: Iran will award buy-back contracts to develop its Soroush and Balal offshore oilfields before the end of March, Seyed Jalilian, director of National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) Offshore, said on Saturday.
"Final proposals of the interested companies have been received by NIOC and the winners will be announced by the end of March," Jalilian told Reuters in an interview in Tehran.
NIOC was comparing technical and financial capabilities of international and Iranian firms to do the work, he said.
Foreign firms that would carry out any major contract work at the two fields could risk falling foul of U.S. President Bill Clinton's Iran-Libya sanctions bill.
The bill, passed last year, gives the president power to sanction non-U.S. firms that invest $40 million or more a year in Iran's vital oil and gas sectors.
Washington has not given few indications on how it will attempt to implement the sanctions bill.
Jalilian would not specify the foreign companies involved but that they were mainly European and Asian.
The Soroush field was badly damaged during the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war and is not currently in production. Output of 90,000 barrels per day (bpd) is expected by the year 2000.
Balal has no production history but is scheduled to produce 40,000 bpd by the end of the decade.
France's Total SA and Malaysian state oil firm Petronas are currently the only foreign companies to be developing Iran's offshore fields under NIOC buy-back formula.
Total signed a groudbreaking $600 million deal with Tehran in 1995 to develop the Sirri E and A oil and gas fields.
The Paris-based firm secured the contract after Clinton barred Houston-based Conoco Inc from carrying out the deal.
